chase: Hm hm, you're on my route now. Come along.
Run if you like. I'll hum the whole way.
I hate waiting, so don't make me wait for you.
Don't stop now. The tune only gets faster from here.
Chase me round the lounge and out the other side.
I'm close now. The hum gets louder when I'm close.
Keep going, little runner. I'll find you by the hum.
Slow down, or I'll be quicker than you think.
Fast is nice, but you'll tire long before I do.
I'll go straight for you, the moment the music fails.
Every corner you turn, the tune turns with you.
Left, then right, then left again. I know this way.
Your shadow just crossed the wall. I'm right behind it.
Stop running. The song says you're mine now.
Closer and closer. Every step you take is a note.
Hmm hmm, lovely shoes. Keep them moving for me.
Follow the tune, dear. It leads straight to you.
Ta-da, I'm on the stairs. Up and up we go.
catch: Got you. Don't squirm, it's only a shoulder carry.
Got you, I think. Hold still while I hum at you.
Hold still and I'll lift you up. That's the shoulder way.
I'll carry you the long way round, up on my shoulder.
Oh, you're mine now. The song is finally in tune.
Caught you. Now the chorus can finally finish.
Don't wriggle. You'll make me drop the beat.
Now you're part of the tune. Come with me, please.
I've got your arm. Walk with me nicely, please.
Dragging you back to the music box. It's not far.
Hold on tight. I'm taking you back to the music.
Shh, one more note and you're mine.
Gently now. I won't hurt you, dear. Just walk.
Your friend is in my arms now. Don't be sad about it.
That's two of you now. The chorus gets bigger.
Hmm, got you. Let's hum the rest together.
Sit down, dear, the music box says you're mine.
Hush now. Your run is over, and the song is done.
hear: Was that a door? Somebody's opening it off-key.
That crash came from the left. I'm going to look.
Something broke over there. Ooh, let me see.
A shout! Lovely. Shouts have a good rhythm.
Footsteps running. I'm already on my way.
I heard a door creak. Creaky doors are my favorite.
Somebody stepped on a squeaky board. Gotcha.
A loud bang from upstairs. I'm going to take a look.
That noise was off the beat. I'll go check it.
Your footsteps came from around that corner. Hello.
Ooh, a clatter in the hall. Off I go.
Someone tripped out there, I think. Coming to see.
There's a rattle in the vent. Hm, that's interesting.
Glass breaking? Please don't be that rude.
Something hit the floor. I'm following the sound.
Something rattled in the cupboard. Hmm, I'll look.
A sneaky step in the hall. Hmm, hmm, who's there?
Glass tinkled upstairs. Oh, that's a new sound.
search: I lost you for a second. Don't do that again.
Silence is awful. Make the music come back, please.
Where did you go? Hm, the hallway is empty.
Nobody here but dust. Dust doesn't hum at all.
I'm sniffing around, but the trail went cold.
Hm. The footsteps stopped. So did you, it seems.
Left the hallway? Hm, that's a shame.
I'll look behind the sofa, then the other side.
Let me check under the stairs. Nobody? Hm.
Quiet down there. Too quiet, actually.
No more footsteps. I'll go back to my tune.
Lost your trail. I'm going to hum while I look.
I'll stop searching when the music is back on.
Nothing here. I'll wander back toward the box.
Maybe you'll come back to me. I can wait a bit.
stunned: Ow! My ears are ringing like a little bell.
Ouch. That was a rude thing to do to a singer.
My arm went numb. Give me a moment, please.
That zap made my hum go all squiggly.
I'm shaking it off. Stop looking at me like that.
Dizzy now. My song is sort of spinning.
You hit me! Fine. My head is still humming, though.
Hold on, I'm still tuning myself back up.
Dizzy, dizzy. My feet don't want to walk straight.
Give me a second. The room is wobbling.
That hit my shoulder. My shoulder is not happy.
I can't hear my own hum right now. That's awful.
Ugh, my fingers are tingling. Pins and needles.
Stop it, I'm recovering. Give me a breath.
That was unfair. I was just starting my chorus.
hide_spot: Hiding behind the music box? That box is mine, you know.
You're hiding well, but your breathing is loud.
Shh, you found the quiet corner. Stay right there.
Is that a locker? Somebody's breathing in there, I think.
Under the bed? Hm, that's a classic. I'll look.
Every hiding spot has a squeak. I can hear yours.
Behind the curtain again? That's the first place I check.
Walking past your spot now. Pretend you're just a chair.
I can see your toes under there. Lovely toes.
I'm opening the locker slowly. Let's see who's inside.
Hiding is not part of the song, you know. Come out.
Quiet is nice, but you're not quiet enough.
I'll knock on the locker in three. One, two, three.
Somebody's in the cupboard. Hello, cupboard person.
Oh, a wardrobe. I always check the wardrobe first.
light: Don't point that flashlight at my music box, please.
Ooh, a flashlight. Pretty. Now it's in my way.
That light on my face makes me sneeze. Stop it.
Turn that flashlight somewhere else, it's blinding me.
I can't see a thing. Everything is white like static.
My eyes are watering. Point it at the floor, please.
Too bright! My eyes are squeezing shut now.
Ow, the light is stinging my eyes. Please, no.
That flashlight is rude. I was humming in the dark.
Everything went white. Hm, I'll wait it out.
I'm dazzled. The room is a blur of bright.
Please stop shining that at my face. I'm trying to hum.
Lamps are a bit too cheerful for my taste.
Bright light makes the song go all sour.
Lights on, lights off. You're making my head spin.
idle: My music box sits in the corner, humming quietly to itself.
Hum with me. No? Fine, I'll hum for both of us.
I like the slow parts best. They give me time to dream.
A song is never really finished. It just waits for you.
The little winding sound is the sweetest thing here.
I've been humming since the day I found my box.
Don't talk over the chorus. Listen to it first.
Quiet is the worst thing in the whole Route, I think.
Do you like music? Everybody likes my song, I think.
The others never listen to music. How sad for them.
Who hasn't heard my song yet? You're missing out.
Hm hm hm, la la, the same four notes again.
Nap time for a few minutes. Don't wake me up.
I'm waiting for a new song to come into my head.
Tap, tap, tap on the rail. That's my rhythm today.
ability: When the box runs down, I stop humming and start hunting.
Wind the box up and I'll stay sweet. Mostly, anyway.
The box stopped. Now I hear every little thing you do.
While the box plays, I wander slowly and never peek.
When the tune winds down, I start peeking round corners.
The tune went off-key, so now I stalk you round corners.
When the box stops, I run to whoever is nearest it.
Every time the music stops, I get faster and crosser.
A calm song never catches anyone. Only a sour one does.
When I peek, I hold my breath and count to three.
Stalking is just humming with your eyes open. Sort of.
While the box plays, I can't catch anyone. Lucky you.
Off-key and sneaky. That's the tune when the box runs low.
Once the box goes quiet, I don't stop until I find you.
No music means I'm quick. Wind it and I slow down.
mechanic: Oh no, the box stopped. Someone wind it, please.
Wind the box up, please. Quiet makes me cross.
Wind the music box nearest you if you want me calm.
A music box runs down by itself. It needs winding.
Winding takes a few turns. Count them with me.
Turn the key slowly. Too fast and the tune breaks.
Hold the box steady while it winds. It hates bumps.
If you break the music box, the whole Route goes quiet.
Stairs are awkward when you're humming. Take them slowly.
Doors that squeak ruin the rhythm. Please oil them.
Radar pings line up with my tune. Ding, ding.
Vents rattle in a funny rhythm. I rather like that.
Batteries hum a little. Is that a note or static?
Falls ruin the song. Watch your step, please.
Route items come and go. Music boxes stay with me.
The music box needs winding before it will play.
Batteries power the box, so keep them safe, dear.
Relay under the piano. Hum while you fix it.
